newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS says alliance wouldn't alter structure.
newsitem.headline: SAS says alliance wouldn't alter structure.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) on Thursday said that any extension of its present alliance with four other carriers would not alter the shape of the carrier's present proprietership.
"A widening of the collaboration would be based on commercial agreements and would not include changes to the ownership structure," a company statement said.
The company had earlier refused to confirm or deny reports from aviation industry sources that it planned to join a new nine-member global air alliance.
"SAS is at the present time involved in bilateral deals with four other airlines and we all obviously discuss the possibility of extending cooperation," spokesman Peter Skaarup told Reuters.
"We are especially interested in widening our alliance with Lufthansa, but no decision has been made on anything at all," he added.
On Wednesday the sources told Reuters that nine major carriers planned a powerful new alliance to counter the proposed link-up between British Airways (BA) and American Airlines.
They said the grouping would build around the core alliance between United Airlines, Lufthansa and SAS.
Airlines mentioned included Thai International, Brazil's Varig, All Nippon Airways, South African Airways, Air Canada and British Midland.
SAS has bilateral alliances already with Lufthansa, Thai International, United Airlines and Air Canada. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969650
